title: Wicflow hero explainer: the work, in blocks (final storyboard)
logline: A company’s work folds into Wicflow’s wireframe block world, and off-the-shelf software won’t sit on it. The AI mapping lifts that work onto the site’s own Week 1 → Week 2 timeline, finds one more process and turns it into a costed plan ranked by return. The plan then lies down as the ground, and its top row rises as the periwinkle first block, guaranteed. Inside that block no open quote goes quiet. Block by block the system builds and lights up as one. For the CTA, the first block’s face seats into the wicflow mark, and then everything unbuilds back into the work so the film loops.

beats.name: The work, as blocks
beats.onScreen: Quotes. / Enquiries. / Hours. / Reports. (one word per line in the left column, each landing with its block)
beats.visual: The background stays still. Four glass work cards (300×200) float where the block world will stand: QUOTE, ENQUIRY, HOURS and REPORT. Each has a small mono tag and abstract content only (placeholder lines, a chat bubble, a timesheet grid, four mini bars), with no invented names or numbers. One by one, each card tips into the isometric plane and becomes a dashed wireframe toy block with a stud as its word lands in the left column. The other ten blocks then draw in around them until the whole 14-block wireframe company stands at the right (x 1000–1720, y 170–971, 74% of the frame height). The card-to-block mapping holds for the whole film: QUOTE → 01 (0,2,0), ENQUIRY → 02 (2,2,0), HOURS → 04 (0,1,1), REPORT → 05 (1,0,1).
beats.motion: 0.00: the cards are already drifting (B15: 6 px and ±1.5° on a 3.76 s period, phase-offset), so frame 0 moves. 0.15: ‘Quotes.’ rises 40 px (A5 slowed, 0.4 s). With it the QUOTE card corner-pins from upright onto block 01’s top-face rhombus (B3, 0.55 s), its contents dissolve into a dashed stud, the side edges draw downward (B11, 0.25 s) and the block lands with a 3 px drift, no overshoot. 0.70: ‘Enquiries.’ with ENQUIRY → 02. 1.25: ‘Hours.’ with HOURS → 04, which hovers at level 1 until the block beneath it draws. 1.80: ‘Reports.’ with REPORT → 05. 2.20–2.80: the other ten blocks stroke-draw outward from block 01 (0.30 s each, 0.03 s stagger). From 2.80 the dashes march (B10, 12 px/s), and they keep marching in every wire beat. A new event lands every 0.55 s.
beats.transitionOut: 3.40–3.60: the four words leave upward (ease-in, 24 px, 0.2 s, 0.04 s stagger). At 3.55 the off-the-shelf slab is already entering from above the frame, so the eye passes from the words to the slab with no gap.

beats.name: Off the shelf never fits
beats.onScreen: Software made to work / for every company (44 px) + never quite / fits yours. (96 px) → swap → Built around / how you work. (96 px) + Custom automation and AI, / not software off the shelf. (44 px)
beats.vo: Off-the-shelf software never quite fits. We build around how you work.
beats.visual: A plain grey slab lowers onto the irregular wireframe company and cannot seat. It is one standard box with a 3×3 footprint, no studs and ‘OFF THE SHELF’ printed on its side. Top block 06 is buried inside it, outlined in thin Wicflow orange, and orange dashed drop lines mark the empty gaps under it. The slab lifts away, and the wireframe tightens while a soft light band reads its real shape. Orange appears only in this beat.
beats.motion: 3.55–4.25: the slab descends from above the frame (offset −620 px) on a long ease-out (B3, 0.7 s), and its soft shadow grows on the blocks beneath. 4.25–4.45: it sinks the last 20 px; the orange intersection outline around 06 draws on (0.2 s) and the slab stops with a damped 4 px settle, no bounce. 4.45–4.80: three orange gap markers drop from its underside (B11, 0.25 s each, 0.05 s stagger). 3.62/3.68: the two support lines rise (A5, 0.4 s). 3.72/3.84: ‘never quite’ / ‘fits yours.’ rise (landed 4.24). 4.80–5.45, kept alive: the markers pulse (B15, 1.2 s), the slab hovers ±2 px and the dashes march. 5.45–5.65: the old text drops out downward (ease-in, 24 px). 5.50–6.05: the slab lifts away on an ease-in (accelerating out) and fades before the top edge, the markers retracting with it. 5.62/5.74: ‘Built around’ / ‘how you work.’ drop in from 60 px above (A2 slowed, 0.4 s ease-out; landed 6.14). 5.76/5.82: the new support rises (landed 6.22). 6.05–6.50: the dashes tighten from 6/6 to 3/4 and from .42 to .55 opacity (B3). 6.25–7.05: a soft white band sweeps the cluster from its left corner to its right corner (B11), lighting the dashes it touches. 7.05–7.40: the stack breathes (levels part 0–4 px). The band’s afterglow stays on the top faces of the four work blocks (01, 02, 04, 05), which warm to rgba(185,193,255,.10).
beats.transitionOut: 7.40–7.60: the headline, then the support, leave upward (ease-in, 0.2 s, 0.04 s stagger). At 7.45 the four warmed top faces lift off their blocks; they are about to become the mapping’s chips.

beats.name: First we map where the time goes
beats.onScreen: Kicker: AI MAPPING · FIXED PRICE · 1–2 WEEKS. Headline: First we map / where the time goes. (second line in PEACH). Timeline: WEEK 1 · WEEK 2. Chips: Quotes · Enquiries · Hours · Reports, plus New customers (found).
beats.vo: First, we map where the time goes.
beats.visual: Kinetic type over the site’s own ‘How we start’ timeline, centred. The top faces of the four work blocks become glass chips carrying the B1 words; the rest of the wireframe undraws, leaving only the still navy. A 1200 px timeline draws under the chips, from a white Week 1 dot to a peach Week 2 dot. A soft periwinkle scan travels the line from Week 1 to Week 2. Each chip it passes is mapped: its border lights and a small heat bar grows under it, a schematic return with no number. In a gap at the far left it finds one more process, ‘New customers’, which draws on dashed and then fills. The 3D world rests for two beats so that it can return through the plan.
beats.motion: 7.45–7.60: the four faces lift 24 px. 7.60–8.20: they fly to the chip row and un-skew from 240×139 rhombi into 64 px glass pills (B2 long S, 0.6 s, 0.05 s stagger), their words fading in. 7.55–8.00: the rest of the wire undraws back to front (stroke retract, ease-in). 7.75–8.15: the kicker types on (A6). 7.85/7.97: the headline lines rise (A5, 0.4 s; landed 8.37), and the PEACH gradient creeps 15% across over 2 s. 8.00–8.50: the timeline draws left to right (B11). The Week 1 dot appears at 8.00 and the Week 2 dot at 8.50 (scale 0 → 1, 0.15 s, no overshoot), and the WEEK labels fade up. 8.55–8.80: the chips slide right to open a gap at the far left (B1, 0.25 s). 8.60–10.20: the scan glow runs from x 360 to x 1560 (B11, 1.6 s). 8.70–9.00: ‘New customers’ draws on dashed (0.15 s) and fills (0.15 s). As the scan reaches each chip (8.86, 9.20, 9.49, 9.77, 10.02), its border turns #B9C1FF for 0.3 s and its heat bar grows (B11, 0.35 s). 10.20–10.50: the Week 2 dot blooms peach (B3).
beats.transitionOut: 10.85–11.05: kicker and headline leave upward (ease-in, 28 px). 10.95–11.55: the chips swing down into a column at the plan’s row positions (B4 spring, 0.05 s stagger), shedding their pills as the text grows from 36 to 44 px. The timeline glides up to y 446 and stretches to x 330–1590 while its dots and labels fade (0.15 s). It becomes the plan’s divider, and the glass card grows out of that line, 276 px up and 484 px down (ARRIVE, 0.5 s).

beats.name: A costed plan, highest return first
beats.onScreen: AI MAPPING · FIXED PRICE · 1–2 WEEKS / A costed plan → Highest return first. / Build first · Returns · Costs / 01 Quote follow-ups [First block] / 02 Enquiries answered / 03 New customers / 04 Hours to invoices / 05 Owner’s weekly report / Example: Kallio Lämpö, a made-up heating company
beats.vo: A costed plan. Highest return first.
beats.visual: A centred glass card shows what the mapping delivers. The chips are now its rows, and each short word drops through to its full Kallio Lämpö block name. The heat bars slide into a Returns column and grow, and a Costs column shows ‘€’ with a schematic bar; there are no digits anywhere. Then the rows physically re-rank by return. The heading drops through to ‘Highest return first.’, the numbers 01–05 step in, and Quote follow-ups, now on top, gets the ‘First block’ tag. A footnote names Kallio Lämpö as the site’s made-up example.
beats.motion: 11.20–11.55: the card completes and the rows settle in the order they were found: New customers, Quotes, Enquiries, Hours, Reports. 11.30–11.70: the mono label types on (A6). 11.35: ‘A costed plan’ rises (A5, 0.4 s; landed 11.75). 11.50–11.95: each short word drops through to its block name (A2, 8 f halves, 0.06 s stagger). 11.70–11.90: column heads and footnote fade in. 11.80–12.40: the heat bars slide into the Returns column (B2, 0.3 s) and grow to full length (B11, 0.35 s, 0.06 s stagger); each cost cell fades up 0.07 s after its bar. 12.40–13.10, kept alive: the card floats ±3 px (B15), and a glint runs along the longest bar at 12.60 (0.4 s). 13.10–13.60, the re-rank by return (B2 long S, 0.5 s, 0.03 s stagger): Quote follow-ups rises to row 1 and Enquiries answered to row 2, both lifted (scale 1.01, shadow 0 12 32 rgba(0,0,0,.45)) and passing in front; New customers sinks to row 3 behind them at 85%. 13.15–13.55: the heading drops through (A2, 0.2 s halves) to ‘Highest return first.’ 13.55–13.85: ‘01’…‘05’ step in (B13, 0.05 s stagger). 13.75–14.05: row 01’s highlight glides in (B4, 0.3 s) and its number turns #B9C1FF. 13.95–14.25: the ‘First block’ tag fades in and scales from 0.96 to 1.0 (B3, no overshoot). 14.25: rows 02–05 dim to 60%. 14.35: a sheen runs along row 01’s return bar (0.5 s).
beats.transitionOut: 14.80–15.00: heading, mono label, column heads, footnote and rows 02–05 leave (ease-in, 0.2 s). 14.85–15.15: row 01 lifts off the card (scale 1.03, its shadow growing to 0 24 60 rgba(0,0,0,.5), B3). At 15.20 the emptied card starts to tilt into the ground.

beats.name: First block, guaranteed
beats.onScreen: Leader label: First block · guaranteed. Headline: If it doesn’t do / what we agreed, / you don’t pay.
beats.vo: First block, guaranteed. Not as agreed? You don’t pay.
beats.visual: The signature flourish, where flat UI turns into the 3D world. The emptied plan card tilts and lies down as the floor of the block world, its rows and columns re-spacing into the 3×3 cells. The lifted top row shrinks onto the first block’s cell, lands flush and extrudes into the periwinkle first block with its stud and glow. The rest of the company draws back in around it as dashed wireframe (reference 1), rippling outward from the first block, and the reference’s thin leader line drops to ‘First block · guaranteed’. The left column states the guarantee in the site’s own words.
beats.motion: 15.20–16.20: the card corner-pins into the floor footprint (B2 long S, 1.0 s, motion blur on the six fastest frames): (300,170) → (1000,762.5), (1620,170) → (1360,554), (1620,930) → (1720,762.5), (300,930) → (1360,971). Its fill fades from .055 to 0, its border turns WIRE, and its five row lines and two column lines re-space into the floor’s 2 + 2 inner lines (the extras fade). 15.40–16.30: the lifted row contracts and corner-pins onto cell (0,2,0)’s footprint, (1120,693) (1240,762.5) (1120,832) (1000,762.5), landing flush as its tint rises to GLASS-PERI (B2, 0.9 s). 16.40–16.70, extrusion: the top face rises 128 px and the side faces grow (ARRIVE, 0.3 s) while the fill goes from GLASS-PERI to PERI; the last 3 px of the rise are the settle. 16.65–16.80: the stud rises 20 px. 16.70–17.10: the glow blooms. 16.70–17.40: the other 13 blocks draw on in WIRE, rippling out from block 01 (0.25 s each, 0.04 s stagger), and the floor lines become their bottom edges. 16.90–17.25: the leader draws down (B11); the dot appears at 17.25 (0.1 s) and the label types on 17.30–17.75 (A6). 17.00/17.12/17.24: the headline lines rise (A5, 0.4 s; landed 17.64). 17.75–19.00, kept alive: the glow breathes (B15, 2.4 s), the dashes march, a glint arc crosses the stud at 18.30, and the label dot pulses once at 18.80.
beats.transitionOut: 19.15–19.35: the headline leaves upward (ease-in); the label stays. 18.95–19.13: block 01 grows from 1.00 to 1.04 about its top-face centre (1120,634.5) (B3). 19.13–19.40: it zooms through ×4 into its top face (B16 whipIn, 16 frames), and the cut to the automation panel falls on the fastest frame.

beats.vo: Then it runs. No open quote goes quiet.
beats.visual: Inside the first block, the quote follow-up automation is running. It uses Wicflow’s glass UI tinted periwinkle, so the block’s colour carries over. The panel takes the cluster’s place and shows the ‘First block’ tag, the title ‘Quote follow-ups’, a green ‘Running’ dot and three open-quote rows made of placeholder lines (no invented names). A highlight steps down the rows. For each one a draft slides out and types itself, and the pill changes from ‘Open’ to ‘Draft ready’. The kinetic touch, taken from Concept B and made true: while the third quote waits, the letters of ‘quiet.’ dim one by one, and when its draft is ready they brighten back. The automation keeps the quote from going quiet.
beats.motion: 19.40–19.67: the panel grows from 25% to 100% about (1360,540) on whipOut (16 frames), with radial motion blur in the first 6. Its contents follow (B9: header 3 frames behind, rows 6). 19.70/19.82: ‘No open quote’ / ‘goes quiet.’ rise (A5, 0.4 s; landed 20.22). 19.80: the Running dot starts pulsing (B15, 1.2 s). 19.90–20.35, row 1: a 2 px #B9C1FF highlight glides in (B4, 0.2 s); a draft card slides 70 px out from behind the document glyph (B3, 0.3 s) and its three lines type on (A6); at 20.25 the pill cross-fades from ‘Open’ to ‘Draft ready’ and widens (B1, 0.2 s). 20.40–20.85: row 2 does the same, with its pill changing at 20.75. 20.60–21.00: the support fades up (B3). 20.90: the highlight reaches row 3. Its time track fills (B11, 20.95–21.80) while the letters of ‘quiet.’ dim to 45% from left to right (0.08 s stagger, 0.3 s each, 21.00–21.70). 21.80–22.15: row 3’s draft slides out and types. 22.15: its pill flips to ‘Draft ready’, and the letters of ‘quiet.’ brighten back to 100% in a soft wave (0.05 s stagger, 22.15–22.50). 22.40–22.90: a sheen runs down the three ‘Draft ready’ pills while the panel breathes 2 px.
beats.transitionOut: 22.85–23.05: the text leaves (ease-in). 22.93–23.20: the panel shrinks into block 01’s top face (reverse zoom-through, whipIn, 16 frames). At the cut (23.20) the world appears at ×4 about (1120,634.5) and settles to ×1 by 23.47 (whipOut), with block 01 glowing in place.

beats.name: One system, all of it connected
beats.onScreen: Headline: One system. Support: In your name and colours. Leader label at the top block: All of it connected. Chips: Hosted in Finland · One contact at Wicflow.
beats.vo: One system, all of it connected, hosted in Finland.
beats.visual: The reference’s finale. Thin periwinkle light lines run between the six named blocks along isometric directions, floating just above the surfaces and converging on top block 06, which turns solid with a brighter glow. A leader rises from it to ‘All of it connected’, as in reference 4. Then comes the second flourish: one bright pulse runs from block 01 through the whole network, lighting every stud in turn, and after that small pulses keep travelling the lines. The left column holds ‘One system.’, the name-and-colours line and two chips saying how it is run.
beats.motion: 27.05: ‘One system.’ lands, formed from the merged list. 26.90–27.90: the light lines draw on in order 01→02, 02→03, 01→04, 03→05, 04→06, 05→06 (B11, 0.4 s each, 0.12 s stagger), each led by a small spark. 27.50–27.90: 06 goes WIRE → GLASS → SOLID with a brighter glow, lands with a 3 px drift and prints ‘06’. 27.70–28.10: the support rises (A5). 27.85–28.15: the top leader draws upward (B11); the dot appears at 28.15 and ‘All of it connected’ types on 28.15–28.55 (A6). 28.20–29.00, the connection pulse: one bright wave travels from 01 through every line to 06 (B11, 0.8 s), and the studs light white as it reaches them. On arrival, 06 gives off a soft halo (0.4 s) and every solid block’s glow steps up 20%. 28.60–28.95: the two chips rise 16 px and fade in (B3, 0.1 s stagger). From 29.00: 12 px pulses travel the lines toward 06 at a constant 240 px/s (B10), three at a time, and the stack breathes.
beats.transitionOut: 30.50–30.75: the text, the chips, the top label and the first-block label leave (ease-in, 0.25 s). The lit, connected cluster stays with its pulses running, and block 01’s top face brightens, about to lift.

beats.vo: (none: the tail of the music bed carries the loop)

The unnamed blocks undraw, and the four work blocks fold back up into the floating QUOTE, ENQUIRY, HOURS and REPORT cards. The work keeps coming, and the loop restarts.

Their side faces retract into the top face (0.2 s), the top face corner-pins upright into its card (B3, 0.45 s), and the card’s contents fade back in. Each card arrives at its frame-0 position and rotation; its B15 drift is layered on the fold path, so it reaches frame 0 with the same pose and velocity.

notes: Verdict and grafts. The base is Concept A. Scores out of 10 (A / B): story clear when muted 8/7, block thread 9/6, variety 6/9, one element becoming the next 8/9, truth 9/6, readability 9/5, loop 8/9, premium dark SaaS fit 8/8. Totals: A 65, B 59. A keeps the block world alive from frame 0 and covers all three flat UI beats the brief asks for (the mapping, a costed plan, a running automation). It also sizes its text for a hero player. B's on-screen problems ('Enquiries pile up', 'Hours re-typed into invoices') are guesses, not site facts. B's block world only arrives at 16 s, and its 18–30 px text is too small for a hero player. Grafted from B: (1) the mapping as kinetic type on the site's own Week 1 → Week 2 timeline, with the work riding on it as chips; (2) the chips becoming the plan's rows and the timeline its divider; (3) a re-rank that shows 'Highest return first'; (4) the signature tilt, where the plan lies down as the floor and its top row rises as the first block; (5) 'All of it connected' at the top block, as in reference 4; (6) one pulse lighting every stud; (7) the fading 'quiet.', which the automation now restores so that it stays true; (8) the first block's face seating into the real wicflow mark. Dropped from A: the scan over the blocks, the mark rebuilt from four faces, and 'Hosted in Finland' as the top label.

Look, from wicflow.com's CSS and references 1–4. Background (BG): one still radial gradient centred (1360,560), #131C3A → #0E1630 (45%) → #0B1220, with 2% static dither. There is no floor grid, and the BG never moves. Text #F3F5FA; muted text rgba(223,230,243,.72); lines rgba(255,255,255,.10). Glass cards: fill rgba(255,255,255,.055–.07), 1 px border rgba(255,255,255,.10–.14), 24 px backdrop blur, even shadow 0 0 40–60 rgba(0,0,0,.35), radius 20–32. PEACH, the site's accent-word gradient: linear-gradient(100deg, #fff 0%, #ffd9c8 60%, #f3a585 100%). Periwinkle #6172F3 for bars and UI highlights, and #B9C1FF for the first block's colour family. Green #16B857 appears only on the 'Running' dot, and orange #FF5A1F only for the off-the-shelf misfit in B2. Leader lines: 1 px rgba(223,230,243,.5) with an 8 px #F3F5FA dot and a Fragment Mono 40 px label in sentence case.

Block rules. Orthographic 2:1 isometric. A lattice point (i,j,h) sits on screen at (1360 + 120(i−j), 554 + 69.5(i+j) − 128h). A block in cell (c,r,k) spans c..c+1, r..r+1 and k..k+1. Its top face is a 240×139 rhombus, its height 128 px, and its stud an 88×51 ellipse, 20 px tall, on the top-face centre. Draw back to front (by c+r, then by k). There are 14 blocks: all nine base cells, level 1 at (0,0), (0,1), (1,0) and (2,0), and level 2 at (0,0). The silhouette spans x 1000–1720, y 170–971 (74% of the frame height). The named blocks are the site's Kallio Lämpö blocks (top-face centre in brackets): 01 Quote follow-ups (0,2,0) (1120,634.5), the first block; 02 Enquiries answered (2,2,0) (1360,773.5); 03 New customers (2,0,1) (1600,506.5); 04 Hours to invoices (0,1,1) (1240,437); 05 Owner's weekly report (1,0,1) (1480,437); 06 One system (0,0,2) (1360,239.5). States follow the story and are never skipped. WIRE: no fill, 1.5 px dashed rgba(223,230,243,.42), dash 6/6, marching at 12 px/s. GLASS: faces rgba(255,255,255,.06/.035/.05) top/left/right, 1.25 px edges rgba(255,255,255,.22). SOLID: top #F2F3FC, left #DCDFF5, right #C2C7EC, stud top #FFFFFF, 40 px glow rgba(185,193,255,.22), and its number on the left face in Fragment Mono 34 px #0B1220 at 35%. The first block alone goes through GLASS-PERI (faces rgba(185,193,255,.24/.14/.10), 1.5 px #B9C1FF edges, 24 px glow rgba(97,114,243,.35)) to PERI (top #CDD3FF, left #B9C1FF, right #98A2F5, stud top #DDE1FF, 60 px glow rgba(97,114,243,.45)). The card-to-block mapping holds for the whole film: QUOTE → 01, ENQUIRY → 02, HOURS → 04, REPORT → 05. New customers (03) is the block the mapping finds. Only block 01 is ever a periwinkle block, and 06 stays dashed until it connects, as in reference 3.

Type and layout. Every headline is Stack Sans Headline 500 at 96 px, tracking −2%, 100 px line pitch, at most about 15 characters a line. Support lines are Inter 44 px in the muted colour, 56 px pitch. Kickers, chips and leader labels are Fragment Mono 40 px; 28–36 px is used only for tags, column heads and the made-up-example footnote, none of which the story depends on. The text column is left-aligned at x 170–950, with the block world at x 1000–1720. The kinetic beat (B3) and the plan (B4) are centred, and the automation panel takes the cluster's place. Nothing essential sits outside x 96–1824, y 54–1026. Every line holds for at least 1.2 s after it lands; this is checked in each beat's timings. Before the Finnish version, check that Stack Sans Headline and Fragment Mono have ä and ö. Finnish runs 25–35% longer, so reflow to three lines or drop to 84 px, never below 80 px.

Motion identity: calm, clean, Apple. Arrivals decelerate (B3 soft start with a long settle; A5 rise slowed to 0.4 s; ARRIVE cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)). Exits accelerate (ease-in, 0.2–0.3 s). Landings end in a 2–4 px drift with no overshoot (B4 spring with damping 200; B9 follow-through 3/6 frames). No bounce, elastic or anticipation, and no camera pans. The only scale moves are the two zoom-throughs of block 01 (B16, 16 frames each way, cut on the fastest frame) and one breath out to 0.96 in the CTA. One movement leads at a time, and a new event lands every 0.5–0.8 s. Holds stay alive: the dashes march, the stack breathes 0–5 px, glows breathe and pulses run. Motion norm: the brief names no target, so plan for the house 7% median (motion_check.py at 60 fps). Thin wire lines barely register, so test B1–B2 first at the animatic stage. Sound: effects lead over a quiet music bed (louder if there is no VO), from films/alumni/sound/lib. Cues: felt clicks as blocks land; a dull thud and a soft 'wrong' tick on the slab; line-draw tones and ticks on the timeline; a card-shuffle swish on the re-rank; a deep whoosh and a plastic thock on the tilt and extrusion; typing ticks and a soft ding for each 'Draft ready'; rising clicks block by block; an arpeggio as the pulse lights each stud; a resolving chord under the CTA; a reverse shimmer into the loop.

Truth, exclusions and loop. Every on-screen phrase comes from wicflow.com. Used as written: 'Software made to work for every company never quite fits yours'; 'Custom automation and AI, not software off the shelf'; 'AI mapping', '1–2 weeks', 'fixed price', 'First we map where the time goes', 'Week 1' and 'Week 2'; 'costed plan', with 'what to build first, what it returns, what it costs' as the columns 'Build first · Returns · Costs'; 'Highest return first'; the five Kallio Lämpö block names and the 'First block' tag; 'First block · guaranteed'; 'No open quote goes quiet', 'Drafts ready for the salesperson'; 'Every block priced in writing before we start'; 'One system', 'All of it connected', 'in your name and colours', 'Hosted in Finland', 'One contact at Wicflow'; 'Let's find the first thing to build', 'Book an AI mapping', '300+ projects built'. Lightly shortened: 'Built around how you work' (from '…around how you actually work') and 'If it doesn't do what we agreed, you don't pay' (from '…you don't pay for it'). The only figures on screen are 1–2 weeks and 300+. The bars carry no digits, the quote rows use placeholder lines, and Kallio Lämpö is labelled as the site's made-up example. EXCLUDED, from Wicflow's current hero: stock footage of real work (a forklift, a tractor) and any other footage, a headline over full-bleed video, a linear drift over stock, and the headline's cycling word. Also out: generic AI imagery, cartoon icons, bounce, and the site's other example companies. Loop: 37.60 ≡ 0.00 (frame 2256 = frame 0). The card drift runs on a 3.76 s period (ten periods per loop), so pose and velocity match at the loop point, and no dashes are on screen at frame 0.

styleframes.source: frames-src/ (frame.html?f=<id> draws each key frame as 1920×1080 SVG with Wicflow’s fonts and mark; render.js renders them with Playwright to site/frames/*.jpg at 1600 px)
styleframes.fonts: Stack Sans Headline, Inter, Fragment Mono and Manrope 800 (the nav wordmark), all from wicflow.com, in films/wicflow/harvest/
deviations: B9 wordmark: set as the site nav actually sets it (site.css .brand: Manrope 800, −4% tracking), at 100 px beside the 156×100 mark, instead of Stack Sans Headline 600 at 68 px.

B3 chips: Inter 500 at 40 px (drawn as 36 px) so every story word stays at 40 px or more. The row is laid out from the measured words, centred on x 960 (26 px padding, 16 px gaps), so chip x positions and the scan point differ a few px from the drawn numbers; the B3 → B4 text growth becomes 40 → 44 px.
B6 pills: ‘Draft ready’ widens to x 1436–1690 and ‘Open’ sits at x 1530–1690; the header ‘First block’ pill is 214 px wide so the mono text fits; ‘Running’ is 40 px.
B2 slab: ‘OFF THE SHELF’ is printed in light grey (rgba(225,230,240,.62)); #0B1220 at 45% disappeared on the translucent grey slab over navy.

WIRE blocks carry a faint navy face tint so hidden edges read faintly through, as in reference 1. SOLID and PERI blocks are drawn above glass and wire, so the first block’s faces read fully through the glass in front, as in references 2–4.

Printed block numbers sit left of the face centre so the B8 light lines, which climb the faces at the centre, never cross them; the studs of solid blocks are drawn over the light lines so each line plugs into its stud.

Drop-throughs at 11.6 and 13.35 are drawn a little further along than specified (the new text nearer its baseline) so the frame stays legible; the lifted rows at 13.35 sit on opaque glass plates that hide the sinking row.
Block 02 at 24.05 is shown mid ‘brightening from the top down’ (solid top, glass base) rather than as a uniform 60% mix.
B6 19.55: the giant PERI top face reads as four small wedges at the frame corners.
